final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse supported by a CHF 30 billion Federal Council loss-protection facility (capped and non-negotiable), SNB emergency liquidity with zero haircuts on broadened collateral (live Friday night), and a coordinated public statement at 07:00 Monday framing the deal as strategic consolidation. CS CEO commits to Sunday client calls showing live borrowing data; SNB issues 20:30 Friday confirmation that facility is operational.
minority_objections: AT1 representative repeatedly demanded explicit contractual language in public statements naming AT1 writedown priority and hard loss caps, fearing creditor hierarchy ambiguity would trigger hedging and litigation
Wealth client demanded same-day disclosure triggers if losses track toward cap, warning silent absorption would cause client flight when discovered
key_conflicts: Messaging contradiction: CS CEO framing as 'strategic consolidation, well-capitalized' vs Federal Council's 'loss protection facility' language—resolved by Federal Council agreeing to lead with acquisition narrative
Disclosure timing: Federal Council wanted to absorb losses below 30B quietly to avoid bailout optics vs creditors demanding transparent cap enforcement
Legal liability: SNB refusing to co-sign deposit guarantee without knowing exact scope and indemnity for Friday night facility disclosure
key_concessions: Federal Council capped state liability at CHF 30 billion absolute with no expansion clause, meeting UBS's downside protection demand
Federal Council agreed to frame Monday statement as 'UBS acquiring Credit Suisse as strategic consolidation' (not bailout language) to align with CS CEO's client messaging
SNB agreed to issue 20:30 Friday public confirmation that CS is drawing on facility, despite legal liability concerns, after securing indemnity language
UBS accepted 50% loss coverage above 5% threshold (later formalized as 30B cap) in exchange for Federal Council public ownership of the rescue decision
red_lines: UBS: loss protection in writing by 21:00 Friday or walk away; Federal Council public statement framing this as systemic policy intervention not opportunistic acquisition
Federal Council: domestic deposits only up to 100K CHF legal limit; 30B cap absolute with no Parliamentary expansion; no unlimited contingent liability
SNB: will not sign deposit guarantee without exact legal scope; will not absorb losses beyond 30B cap without written Federal Council commitment
CS CEO: Monday statement must name UBS as definitive acquirer (not 'in negotiation') or client calls create contradiction and trigger run
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Retail and mid-market depositor behavior Sunday night—room focused on top-50 client calls and funding desk outreach but no concrete plan for mass retail communication until very late
Systems execution risk—CS operations team committing to post live borrowing data by 21:00 Friday with only 4 hours notice, no discussion of failure scenarios
AT1 creditor legal challenge risk—repeatedly raised by AT1 rep but never resulted in binding contractual language in public statements, only in internal loss schedule
Q2 loss tracking and cap breach—room agreed on 30B ceiling but left disclosure trigger for losses approaching cap vague despite creditor demands
downstream_risk_variables: Whether CS operations actually delivers live borrowing portal data by 21:00 Friday—if delayed, Sunday client calls fail
Whether Federal Council's Monday 07:00 statement language exactly matches CS CEO's Sunday client messaging—any drift triggers depositor confusion
Whether SNB's 20:30 Friday facility confirmation is interpreted as confidence signal or panic signal by markets
Whether AT1 holders challenge the loss waterfall in court despite signed schedule, exploiting ambiguity in public statement language
Whether actual losses track toward 30B cap by Q2 and Federal Council faces Parliamentary pressure to expand despite contractual prohibition
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved procedural convergence (signed loss schedule, coordinated statements, facility activation) but left three substantive uncertainties unresolved: (1) whether the 'strategic consolidation' framing will hold when depositors see loss-protection facility details, (2) whether retail/mid-market depositors not on Sunday calls will interpret Friday/Monday signals as strength or managed failure, (3) whether AT1 creditors will litigate the hierarchy despite signed schedule, exploiting the gap between internal documentation and public statement language.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Wealth client R1: 'If deposits aren't safe by Monday open, the facility doesn't matter—fifty billion sits idle while the run accelerates.' Federal Council immediately pivoted to deposit guarantee + acquisition structure, not liquidity alone.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS CEO R1 demanded Federal Council public ownership of rescue as condition of acquisition; by R3 UBS confirmed 'Acquisition is live Monday morning' with signed loss schedule. This path became the binding solution.
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council committed CHF 30B loss-protection cap (R3-R9), SNB activated zero-haircut facility (R5), and Federal Council agreed to co-sign Monday statement framing rescue as systemic policy intervention (R4-R9). Government backing was non-negotiable precondition for UBS.
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client R1 demanded written deposit guarantee; CS CEO R6-R10 organized Sunday calls to top-50 clients to prevent withdrawals; SNB R10 issued 20:30 Friday facility confirmation specifically to stop Sunday run. Client flight drove the entire Friday-Sunday communication strategy.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 rep raised writedown priority and creditor hierarchy in R2, R3, R6, R9 but never forced contractual language into public statements—only internal loss schedule. Acknowledged as risk but did not change public messaging or cap structure.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep R2 demanded clarity on whether AT1 burns before state absorbs; FINMA R3 proposed waterfall (AT1 first, subordinates second, state cap 30B). Conflict was resolved in internal documentation but public statement left hierarchy vague per Federal Council preference.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep R3, R6, R9 warned creditors would challenge deal if public statement left hierarchy ambiguous; Federal Council rejected binding disclosure language to preserve messaging flexibility. Risk acknowledged but not mitigated in public-facing documents.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Federal Council R1 demanded legal documentation 'before market open'; UBS R2 set 21:00 Friday deadline for loss protection or walk; FINMA R3 required signed schedule by 20:45; SNB R10 issued 20:30 facility confirmation. Friday night deadlines drove every major decision and concession.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Discussed throughout (e.g., Federal Council R1 'distinction matters Monday morning'; CS CEO R5 'clients need to hear confidence') but did not force a specific decision—room already committed to Monday 07:00 statement and acquisition announcement by R4. Risk shaped messaging tone but not structure.
